title.en: Trade and crafts of the Indus people

text.en:
Long ago in Lothal a craftsman made beads from carnelian, a red stone. He drilled tiny holes with great care.
A trader packed them in a bundle to carry by boat to far lands.
"These beads will travel across the sea," he said.

The Indus people were skilled craftspeople. They made pottery on wheels, bead necklaces, copper and bronze tools and cotton cloth. They carved small stone seals with animals and signs.
They traded with each other and with far lands such as Mesopotamia. Goods travelled by bullock cart and boats. Lothal had a dockyard where ships could be loaded.
Seals were used to stamp goods, like a mark of the owner. We still cannot read the Indus script, so many things about them remain a mystery.
The Indus people made pottery, beads, copper tools and cotton cloth.
They carved small stone seals with animals and signs.
They traded with faraway lands by bullock cart and by boat. Lothal had a dockyard.
We cannot yet read the Indus script, so we still have many questions.

problem.en: How do we know the Indus people traded with distant lands?

text.en: Indus seals and beads have been found in Mesopotamia.
Lothal had a dockyard for ships.
So they traded with far lands.

prompt.en: A friend asks what a seal was used for. How will you explain?

requiredIdeas.en: It was a small stone stamp with a picture and signs.
It marked goods to show who owned them.

points.en: Indus people made pottery, beads, tools and cloth.
They traded by land and sea; Lothal had a dockyard.
Seals marked goods; the script is not yet read.
